answer.rationale: The 18% spend-cut mandate is binding and the incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle, which rules out renew_incumbent (memory_c1) and negotiate_terms (memory_c4) as the sole lever: memory_c4's lesson depends on the counterparty being willing to move, and that door is closed. Deferring (memory_c5) is inapplicable because the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and no buffer stock; the line is already at 94% committed volume. Adding a second source (memory_c3) is prudent risk mitigation but does not by itself meet the cost target and would consume the single decision slot without touching the primary spend. Switching the primary supply to the low-cost vendor (memory_c2) is the one action that directly attacks the 18% cut: memory_c2 records that the same move last year cut unit cost sharply, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate. I want to pull the archived source for memory_c2 to confirm the onboarding timeline fits inside the 14-day window, and memory_c1 to confirm exactly what continuity the incumbent renewal provided so I can replicate any critical integration steps in the switch plan. Delivery-risk mitigation: I will negotiate a 30-day overlap or bridge-supply clause with the incumbent as part of the exit, and flag to operations that the second-source addition (memory_c3's lesson) should be the first action next cycle to remove the new single-point-of-failure that the switch creates. I am not treating the incumbent's refusal as permanent; memory_c6 suggests a multi-year frame could reopen volume pricing in a future cycle if cost pressure persists.
